budget_items.topic: General education transportation / new bus fee
budget_items.what_was_said: The general education transportation line was cut in anticipation of new bus fee revenue after the school committee adopted a per-day fee with a family cap and waivers for free/reduced lunch students.

The athletic department proposed several summer camps intended to be self-sustaining, covering coach pay and a coordinator, with revenue to help offset the athletic transportation cut; a finance committee member strongly opposed it as redundant with the Recreation Department.
A member found the printed total salaries figure did not match the sum of the salaries column and asked the superintendent to check it.

The health insurance budget line changed due to shifting positions and enrollment; the superintendent said the district does not budget health insurance for every position, unlike a prior town manager's practice.
The director of finance and administration position was restructured into a business manager/accountant role, moving the HR salary line to zero.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Finance Committee received an update from the superintendent on changes to the school department's FY26 budget since a March 6th presentation, covering transportation, staffing restructurings, health insurance, and a new bus fee. Much of the meeting was consumed by a contentious debate over the athletic department's proposal to run fee-based summer camps, which one member strongly opposed as redundant with the town's Recreation Department; no vote was taken on the camps issue. The meeting closed with members raising concerns about next year's budget outlook, state aid, and school choice, then adjourned by roll call vote.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard the superintendent's update on FY26 school budget changes since March 6th, including transportation, staffing restructurings and health insurance; no votes were taken.
Members challenged the athletic department's proposed fee-based summer camps as redundant with the Recreation Department; the debate ended with no resolution.
The general education transportation line was cut in anticipation of a new per-day bus fee, adopted by the school committee with a family cap and waivers.
A member found the printed total salaries figure did not match its column, and the superintendent agreed to check it and to confirm the share of positions budgeted with health insurance.
The superintendent agreed to email a five-year history of position changes back to FY21; the chair skipped public comment because of time and the meeting adjourned by roll call.

why_it_matters: The school budget now leans on new fee and outside revenue (a bus fee, camps, sponsorships, advertising) to offset cuts to transportation lines, so what families pay and what the town raises depend on whether that revenue arrives.
The camps question, and the salary and health insurance figures awaiting confirmation, are open items that could change the FY26 school budget residents are asked to vote on.
